newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares end higher on hopes of end to crisis.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares end higher on hopes of end to crisis.

text.p: Delhi share prices closed sharply higher on Tuesday in line with rising expectations that the ruling United Front coalition and the Congress party would resolve the nation's political crisis, brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's sensitive index reversed course to close 7.72 points higher at 753.40 points.
News that Congress president Sitaram Kesri was willing to hold talks with Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's ruling coalition sparked buying.
"Reports that the Congress party president Sitaram Kesri has softened his stand towards the United Front coalition government fuelled a fresh spell of speculative buying," said one broker.
Kesri said that he was ready to hold talks with the United Front coalition provided the ruling alliance came forward with a proposal.
Later, the United Front said formal talks would start on Wednesday morning.

Kesri triggered a political crisis on March 30 when he announced the withdrawal of Congress's vital support to Deve Gowda's minority government. Deve Gowda faces a vote of confidence in parliament on Friday.
Brokers said heavy buying by domestic financial institutions also aided the recovery in share prices.
"Sizeable purchases by the largest financial institution, the Unit Trust of India, helped lift share prices," said B.K. Nagpaul of brokers B.B. Portfolios.
Reliance Industries ended 5.15 rupees higher at 269.00 rupees on late buying by domestic financial institutions, brokers said.
State Bank of India closed 6.70 rupees higher at 272.95.
